name: Heat Wave
lede: Heat Wave is a vivid, fully saturated orange, a name from the modern lists of fashion and crayon shades, with no recorded author or date.

sections.title: A name with no recorded origin
sections.body:
Our sources record the name only on Wikipedia's lists of colors, and ISCC-NBS would call the swatch vivid orange [1]. None of the books read mention it as a color, so who named it, and when, is undocumented [1]. One book does mention a heatwave, but only as a danger to cochineal insects, which die in frost or sustained heat, and that has nothing to do with this orange [2].

Its plain-word relatives are [[orange]], [[safety-orange]] and [[tangerine]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Only one painting in our archive of 23,781 holds this color, and it is rarer than 86 per cent of named colors [3]. A screen-bright orange like this is far from the muted colors of aged, varnished paint, and these archive numbers are photographs of such works, so they describe museums, not painting as a whole [3]. The archive counts a painting only when the color covers a measurable share of its canvas, within a small color distance of the swatch [3].
